Read the announcement Use cases Scripts Pricing Blog Docs Community Sign In Use cases Amazon AI shopping agent E-Commerce Updated Sep 27, 2026 Amazon AI shopping agent: let an AI agent find, compare and buy on Amazon for you Prompt template Find the best product on Amazon under budget , based on recent reviews. Show me your pick and the checkout (address, delivery date, total), and place the order when I say yes. Get started for free Overview Buying the right thing on Amazon takes longer than it should. You compare a dozen listings, you do not trust the star ratings, you read reviews to find the problem nobody mentions in the title, and then you still have to go through checkout and check the address, the delivery date and the total. Why it's hard Amazon has no API for shoppers. The ratings hide as much as they show, and the detail that decides it is often on page three of the reviews. Checkout also changes from one order to the next: another address can be selected, delivery options change the price, and import fees can appear. An agent that only finds a product leaves all of this to you, and an agent that buys without showing you the checkout is not one you can trust with your card. How Reduck does it Your AI agent works in your own browser, where you are already signed in to Amazon. It searches the category, compares the listings and reads the recent reviews, so its pick comes with reasons, not only a rating. Then it opens the checkout for that product and shows you what Amazon shows: the delivery address, the payment method, the delivery options and the order total. You say yes, and it places the order and gives you the order number. You say no, and nothing is bought. What your agent does Search Amazon for the product you describe, within your budget Read the recent reviews of the best candidates and keep the recurring points Tell you its pick and why Open the checkout and show you the address, the payment method, the delivery date and the total Place the order when you confirm, and give you the order number Tell you if your bank asks you to approve the payment, and cancel the order if you change your mind before it ships Who it's for Anyone who wants the research and the checkout done, but keeps the last word Busy people who buy the same kinds of things again and again Ops and office managers who order supplies for a team Scripts used Search products Amazon Get product reviews Amazon Buy now Amazon Get checkout information Amazon Place order Amazon Cancel order Amazon FAQ Will it buy something without asking me? No. Your agent stops on the checkout page and shows you what Amazon shows: the address, the payment method, the delivery options and the order total. It places the order only after you confirm. Which address and card does it use? The ones saved in your Amazon account, the same ones you see at checkout. Your agent reads them back to you before it orders, so you can check them. What if my bank asks me to approve the payment? Some banks ask for an approval in their app (3-D Secure). Your agent tells you when that happens, and gives you the order number, so you can approve it or cancel the order. Can I cancel an order my agent placed? Yes. While the order has not shipped, your agent can cancel it from Your Orders, like you would. Does this need the Amazon API? No. Your agent works in your own signed-in browser, on the same pages you would open yourself. Can it reorder things I buy often? Yes. Ask your agent to reorder something you bought before, and it finds the product, opens the checkout and waits for your yes. For the same items on a fixed schedule, Amazon's own Subscribe & Save is simpler. Is an AI agent allowed to shop on Amazon for me? Your agent works in your own browser, signed in as you, and every order is one you confirm at checkout, like shopping yourself. Amazon's Conditions of Use apply to you as they always do; decide whether that fits how you use your account. Does it just trust the star rating? No. It reads the recent reviews and tells you the points that come back again and again, good and bad. Read the announcement Use cases Scripts Pricing Blog Docs Community Sign In Scripts Search Amazon products amazon.com Search Amazon products Automatically search Amazon products on amazon.com. Search Amazon by free-text query, with Amazon's own filters: department, sort order, price range, and the refinements of its left column (Prime, delivery speed, brand, customer reviews, condition, seller and the product's attributes), whose values List Amazon search filters gives. Returns one page of results: query, page, zip, url, has_next_page and items (asin, title, url, price, list_price, rating, review_count, image_url, sponsored, formats). formats lists each edition a result links to (for example Hardcover, Kindle and Audiobook for a book), with its own ASIN, URL and price when shown. has_next_page is false on the last page, on a page past the last one (Amazon stops near page 20) and when nothing matches; then Amazon can still show a few unrelated sponsored products. Organic results are stable per page but sponsored slots rotate between fetches. Try for free Updated 10/22/26, 3:10 PM · v17 Author reduck Official Input query required Free-text search query. page optional Result page (about 16 to 22 organic results a page; Amazon stops near page 20). has_next_page says when to stop. Default: 1 sort optional Sort order: relevanceblender (featured, the default), price-asc-rank, price-desc-rank, review-rank (average customer review), date-desc-rank (newest arrivals), exact-aware-popularity-rank (best sellers). zipCode optional US ZIP used to pin the store location (prices, availability). Default: "10001" price_max optional Maximum price in US dollars. price_min optional Minimum price in US dollars. department optional Department to search in, as its search alias, e.g. "stripbooks" (Books) or "electronics" (values from list_search_filters, key department). Default: all departments. refinements optional Filters from Amazon's left column, each as group:value, e.g. "p_85:2470955011" (Prime) or "p_123:3271" (a brand). Get them from list_search_filters for the same query. Values of one group are alternatives; different groups all apply. Output url required zip required page required items required The results in page order, sponsored ones included. When nothing matches the query, Amazon can still show a few sponsored products that are not about it. query required has_next_page required True when Amazon offers a next page of results for this search. False on the last page, on a page past the last one, and when nothing matches the query. FAQ What does "Search Amazon products" do? Search Amazon by free-text query, with Amazon's own filters: department, sort order, price range, and the refinements of its left column (Prime, delivery speed, brand, customer reviews, condition, seller and the product's attributes), whose values List Amazon search filters gives. Returns one page of results: query, page, zip, url, has_next_page and items (asin, title, url, price, list_price, rating, review_count, image_url, sponsored, formats). formats lists each edition a result links to (for example Hardcover, Kindle and Audiobook for a book), with its own ASIN, URL and price when shown. has_next_page is false on the last page, on a page past the last one (Amazon stops near page 20) and when nothing matches; then Amazon can still show a few unrelated sponsored products. Organic results are stable per page but sponsored slots rotate between fetches. How do I automatically search Amazon products on amazon.com? Ask an AI agent connected to Reduck to run reduck/amazon.com/search-products, or run it from a terminal with the Reduck CLI: npx @reduck-ai/cli@latest run --script reduck/amazon.com/search-products Is there a amazon.com API to search Amazon products? You do not need one. "Search Amazon products" drives the real amazon.com pages in a browser, so it works whether or not amazon.com offers an API for this. What information do I need to provide? Required: query. Optional: page, sort, zipCode, price_max, price_min, department, refinements. What does it return? It returns url, zip, page, items, query, has_next_page. Do I need to be logged in to amazon.com? No. It only uses pages of amazon.com that are reachable without signing in. Does it change anything on amazon.com, or only read data? It only reads. It looks things up on amazon.com and changes nothing there. How do I run it? Ask an AI agent connected to Reduck to run reduck/amazon.com/search-products, or run it from a terminal with the Reduck CLI: npx @reduck-ai/cli@latest run --script reduck/amazon.com/search-products Who maintains it? Why it's hard The good sources sit behind logins and paywalls, cap free searches, and none of them talk to each other. Joining a company across databases, then chasing its rounds, its investors and its news, is a lot of tabs for one row in a spreadsheet, which is why market maps are usually out of date. How Reduck does it Reduck runs the search in your own session on each platform, then follows each company through to its funding history, investors and recent coverage, and brings it back as one structured set. Your agent does the joining across sources so you get a filled-in list instead of a pile of tabs. The same prompt refreshes the whole map whenever you need it current.
